lines.text: Do you know how your phone finds you indoors, where GPS can't reach? It listens to the Wi-Fi around you.
GPS needs a clear view of satellites. Inside buildings their faint signals fade out, so your phone looks for other clues.
Every Wi-Fi router broadcasts a unique ID, even if you never connect to it. Your phone can hear dozens of them.
Apple and Google keep huge maps of where those routers are. Match the ones your phone hears, and it can place you within tens of meters.
Cell towers help too. How strongly you hear each tower narrows down where you are, though less precisely.
And even a website, with no permission at all, can often guess your city from your internet address.
Orbi only works with a rough area, a cell about forty kilometers wide. People nearby never see your exact spot, just the area.
